subject: Activation cadence and term addendum for Acme Health expansion
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Melissa Gomez <mgomez@acmehealth.com>, InfraOps Team <infraops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Activation cadence and term addendum for Acme Health expansion

Melissa / InfraOps —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our call, I put together a proposed activation cadence and commercial path for accommodating the three new projects your teams want to enable (Athena, Beacon, Cedar). High level: we recommend a phased activation with a pilot canary for Athena, parallel onboarding for Beacon, and delayed activation for Cedar (security review).

Key asks from your side:
- Confirmation of which project to pilot (we recommend Athena).
- Procurement timeline / PO contact so we can align billing and update committed capacity.
- Confirmation you want separate API keys per project + per environment (prod/staging).

Proposed technical approach (short):
- Per-project, per-environment API keys (prod/stage) scoped to service accounts.
- Canary window (2 weeks) for Athena with 10% traffic; automatic rollback trigger if latency >250ms P95 or error rate >2%.
- Beacon onboarding parallel but with lower initial token budget and higher caching configs.
- Cedar held pending compliance sign-off — we’ll queue the onboarding checklist in the shared Drive.

Commercial ask: to support the burst and predictable throughput across the three projects we recommend a committed capacity increase of +40% over current commit and a 12‑month addendum to the existing term. For that increase we are offering an 8% uplift discount on the incremental commit (detail in attached term_addendum_draft.pdf). If you prefer a 6‑month ramp instead of immediate commit, we can provide a phased pricing schedule.

Attachments: acme_rollout_matrix_v2.xlsx (activation timeline + token budget), term_addendum_draft.pdf

Next steps: can you confirm pilot project and share PO contact by EOD Wednesday? Once we have that we’ll kick legal and set the kickoff for the pilot week.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear plan and attachments. A few quick clarifications from procurement and infra:

1) Keys & environments — we do want separate keys per project and per environment (prod/stage), but we prefer the staging keys to be short‑lived (7 days) until the pilot passes.
2) Billing — our procurement team will need a clear line item for the committed uplift and a PO to match. What's the exact dollar amount for the +40% commit under the 8% incremental discount?
3) Timeline — we can start the Athena pilot mid‑November, but Beacon needs a security review before full activation; Cedar will likely be Q1 next year.

I will loop procurement when we have the precise pricing. My procurement contact is: 
Donna Liao (Procurement) <donna.liao@acmehealth.com>, she handles PO issuance and typically needs 7–10 business days for standard addenda.

For the keys: can we get a short write up of the recommended key lifecycle and RBAC model so my infra team can preconfigure?

Melissa
VP Product, Acme Health
mgomez@acmehealth.com

Melissa — thanks, great questions. Short answers and an updated plan below.

Pilot + Keys
- Agree on Athena pilot mid‑November. We’ll issue two keys for the pilot (staging short‑lived 7d, prod canary key with restricted quota).
- Post‑pilot we’ll create per‑project, per‑env keys with service account scoping (recommended: separate consumer service account per project; infra can map those to internal roles).

Key lifecycle + RBAC (summary for InfraOps):
- Staging: keys TTL 7 days, auto-rotate; minimal quota, used only for smoke tests.
- Prod (canary): key scoped to a canary service account with throttles (10% traffic cap during pilot).
- Prod (full): long‑lived keys issued after pilot acceptance, bound to a production service account and attached to the org‑level quota.
- Admin keys: a single admin key (multi‑sig required) for provisioning only; rotate every 30 days.

Operational thresholds (to embed in canary):
- Latency: P95 <250ms expected; alert if >300ms for 5m window.
- Errors: >2% 5m error rate triggers automated fallback to smaller model variant.

Commercials (numbers are illustrative; exact line items attached in updated matrix):
- Current commit: 1.2B tokens/month. Proposed commit: 1.68B tokens/month (+40%).
- Incremental charge at list rate before discount: $0.005/token; incremental discount on the +40% portion: 8%.
- Estimated incremental monthly cost after discount: $1,968 (please see attached spreadsheet for line‑by‑line).
- Term extension: +12 months attached as an addendum (draft attached).

Legal / PO path
- Laura, can you take the addendum draft and generate a redline we can send to Acme legal?
- Melissa, once procurement confirms PO timeline we can queue the finance onboarding and schedule the pilot kickoff.

Attachments: acme_rollout_matrix_v2.xlsx (updated with pilot dates), term_addendum_draft.pdf

If this looks good I’ll ask Sales Ops to produce the formal quote and have Legal push initial redlines.

Thanks —
Rachel
